parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The process timed out with an empty final response and killed workflow state, but the submitted artifact passed the official 115/115 evaluation.

The concrete task-solving difference is process shape rather than final quality. Parallel distributed the port into module children and then recovered manually after the workflow lifecycle broke; serial kept the whole task in one actor and finished normally.

outcome_analysis.causal_scope: No outcome differential; retained label describes an adverse parallel process consequence only.

candidates.reason: The workflow explicitly assigned implementation ownership to four module children for pyint, pyrepr, argparse, and iterutils.
The assembly child was instructed to read all four modules, fix integration problems, and make the whole entry point run.
Final assembly was explicitly assigned to the assemble+smoke child, so the later lifecycle failure is not missing ownership.
The workflow itself owned the end-to-end transition across implementation, assembly, fuzz, audit, fix, and final return.
The parent performed useful preflight probing, but it did not hold all productive implementation behind a mandatory idle gate that caused unfinished work.
Investigation preceded workflow launch, but implementation, assembly, and verification still proceeded and produced a passing artifact.
The assembly path was on the critical path, but the direct evidence is repeated child interruption rather than capacity diverted to auxiliary work.
The fan-out and retry budget pressure is downstream of the same assembly interruption chain, so it is not retained as a separate load-imbalance episode.
The assembly child had broad scope, but the observed adverse event is explicit interruption before return, not proof that the scope itself was too large to checkpoint.
The delegated briefs included the task, file placement, exports, parsing requirements, validation expectations, and delivery constraints known at the time.
The workflow specified module file names, export names, import expectations, and assembly responsibilities, so incompatible work was not caused by an absent contract.
No known requirement or finding is shown disappearing across a summary or transfer; returned module summaries were visible in the journal.
The handoffs were long but structured and were consumed by the parent or assembly child rather than left unusably unprocessed.
No child or parent acted on a handoff that had been superseded by a newer observable workspace state.
The child summaries did not present incompatible contracts that remained unadjudicated at integration time.
The parent did not falsely accept an unresolved integrated mismatch; the official artifact passed and the parallel final response was empty after timeout.
The assembly retries did repeat the assignment, but they could read the current /output state and the successful retry used existing modules and traceback state.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: The assembly child owned entry-point integration and verification, but multiple active assembly attempts were interrupted and the workflow ended killed with no structured aggregate result.
candidates.realized_consequence: The workflow lost its structured assembly return and never completed the planned workflow fuzz, audit, or fix aggregate before the parallel process timed out.
candidates.near_match_reason: The parent independently inspected, tested, and repaired the deliverable enough for official success, so the direct retained boundary is interruption before child result finalization.

candidates.reason: A promotable deliverable was already placed in /output and passed official evaluation; the missing piece was the killed workflow return, not late artifact placement.
No behavior-changing child result is shown being merged after the relevant final integrated verification without a later check; the visible post-check edit was not the retained lifecycle issue.
The completed implementation modules were available in /output and were read or used by the assembly and parent verification paths.
The planned fuzz and audit verifier phases never produced concrete findings to trap below the parent; their absence is downstream of the killed workflow chain.
The parent did take over enough of the unfinished workflow scope by polling output, reading modules, running a differential suite, and surfacing bugs; official evaluation passed.
Completed implementation child results were visible and then used by assembly or parent inspection, not ignored at a decision point.
The parent repeatedly polled /output, read generated modules, smoke-tested the entry point, and ran an independent suite rather than passively waiting.
The separately written modules had assigned responsibilities and no competing cross-file design conflict requiring unresolved reconciliation.
No two live agents are shown concurrently editing the same source file and forcing reconciliation of another active writer's change.
Assembly edits to library files were within its integration authority and did not replace an active owner's source in a way that caused a concrete adverse result.
There is no evidence that competing live agents overwrote the required entry deliverable while another agent owned or used it.
No broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion replaced multiple current outputs and invalidated another agent's final-tree work.
Multiple agents wrote under /output, but the observed result was coordinated component assembly and no separate unstable-state or provenance problem cleared the gate.
No generated temporary artifact or auxiliary implementation from one actor was consumed as a misleading reference environment by another actor.

retained_patterns.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing
retained_patterns.reason: The parallel workflow delegated assembly and smoke verification to a child, then explicitly interrupted repeated active assembly attempts and ended the workflow killed before a structured aggregate result could return.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: The workflow lost its structured assembly return and never completed the planned workflow fuzz, audit, or fix aggregate before the parallel process timed out.
retained_patterns.near_match_reason: The parent did partial takeover and official evaluation passed, so the unrecovered event is not a failed scope left wholly untaken; it is the premature termination of the delegated assembly lifecycle.

deduplicated_same_label_episodes: The three assembly attempts are treated as one retry chain rather than multiple Early Child Termination labels.
suppressed_same_chain_candidates: Fan-out Budget Exhaustion, Oversized Child Task, Blind Timeout Wait, Checkpoint-Free Retry, Missing Verifier Return, and No Failure Takeover were considered but rejected as downstream or weaker readings of the same assembly interruption chain.
